text.en: In Murasaki's phonemic analysis of Sakhalin Ainu, vowel-initial syllables are not recognized, and a weak glottal consonant phoneme *'* is posited before all vowels ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--in-this-phonemic-analysis-of-sakhalin-ainu-vowel⟧. This phoneme is realized as [ʔ] at syllable onset and as weak laryngeal tension intervocalically, yet /V'V/ and /VV/ remain distinctly contrasted ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--the-glottal-stop-is-at-syllable-onset-and⟧. A morpheme-initial *'* is deleted after *-n*, yielding the sequences *-nV-* or *-niV-* ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--a-morpheme-initial-glottal-stop-is-deleted-after⟧.
text.ja: 村崎による樺太アイヌ語の音素分析においては母音で始まる音節は認められず、母音の前には微弱な喉子音音素*'*が立つと考えられる⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--in-this-phonemic-analysis-of-sakhalin-ainu-vowel⟧。この音素は音節頭では[ʔ]として、母音間では弱い喉頭の緊張として実現されるが、/V'V/と/VV/ははっきりと区別される⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--the-glottal-stop-is-at-syllable-onset-and⟧。形態素頭の*'*は*-n*の後で消去され、*-nV-*または*-niV-*となる⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--a-morpheme-initial-glottal-stop-is-deleted-after⟧。

text.en: Vowel-initial syllables phonetically take an onset glottal stop across Ainu generally ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--onset-glottal-stop-before-vowels⟧. In Hokkaido southwest dialects, /ʔ/ occurs syllable-initially when there is no other initial consonant ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--the-glottal-stop-occurs-syllable-initially-when-there⟧. In Sakhalin Ainu, vowel-initial syllables are analyzed as having an onset /ʔ/, yielding C1V, C1VV, or C1VC2 structures ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--in-sakhalin-ainu-vowel-initial-syllables-are-analyzed⟧, and the same analysis applies in Kuril Ainu, where such syllables are treated as C1V or C1VC2 ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--in-kuril-ainu-syllables-beginning-with-a-vowel⟧. The glottal stop [ʔ] is pronounced by breaking the transition between vowels or between a consonant and a vowel ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--the-glottal-stop-is-pronounced-by-breaking-the⟧. Nakagawa, however, asserts that the glottal stop does not distinguish lexical meaning word-initially, as in [e] versus [ʼe], or across consonant-vowel boundaries, as in [itakʼan] versus [itakan] ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--the-glottal-stop-does-not-distinguish-lexical-meaning⟧.
text.ja: アイヌ語全般において、母音で始まる音節の初頭には音声的に声門閉鎖音が現れる⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--onset-glottal-stop-before-vowels⟧。北海道南西方言では、他に頭子音がない場合に音節頭に/ʔ/が生じる⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--the-glottal-stop-occurs-syllable-initially-when-there⟧。樺太アイヌ語では母音で始まる音節は頭に/ʔ/を持つと分析され、C1V、C1VV、あるいはC1VC2の音節構造となり⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--in-sakhalin-ainu-vowel-initial-syllables-are-analyzed⟧、千島アイヌ語においても同様に、母音始まりの音節はC1VまたはC1VC2として扱われる⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--in-kuril-ainu-syllables-beginning-with-a-vowel⟧。声門閉鎖音[ʔ]は、母音と母音の間、または子音と母音の間を区切って発音される⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--the-glottal-stop-is-pronounced-by-breaking-the⟧。しかし中川は、語頭における声門閉鎖音の有無（例：[e]と[ʼe]）や子音・母音間での有無（例：[itakʼan]と[itakan]）が語の意味を区別することはないと主張する⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--the-glottal-stop-does-not-distinguish-lexical-meaning⟧。

text.en: The phonemic status of the glottal stop is disputed. Nakagawa asserts that it is not an independent phoneme but a phonetic boundary marker indicating a syllable boundary before a vowel, and that it has no contrastive function in monomorphemic forms ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--glottal-stop-boundary-marker-not-phoneme⟧⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--in-ainu-the-glottal-stop-has-no-contrastive⟧. Refsing reports that Kirsten Refsing (1986) does not recognize the existence of the glottal stop in Ainu at all ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--kirsten-refsing-1986-does-not-recognize-the-existence⟧, while Refsing also reports that Asai (1969) recognizes glottal closure but does not treat it as a separate phoneme ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--asai-1969-recognizes-glottal-closure-seimon-heisa-but⟧. By contrast, Refsing reports that Hattori (1964) posits a glottal plosive /ʔ/ before all word-initial vowels and intervocalically, treating it as a separate consonant phoneme *'* ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--hattori-1964-posits-a-glottal-plosive-before-all⟧, and Nakagawa reports that in the 1950s Hattori and Tamura similarly recognized the glottal stop as a phonemic consonant occurring before all vowels ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--in-the-1950s-shiro-hattori-and-suzuko-tamura⟧. Satō proposes that the glottal stop can be analyzed as a phoneme before word-initial vowels and between vowels, surfacing as throat tension or as an intervocalic vocal break ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--glottal-stop-can-be-analyzed-as-a-phoneme⟧. Nakagawa notes that recognizing the glottal stop as a phonemic consonant eliminates vowel-initial syllables and simplifies the syllable template of Hokkaido Ainu to CV and CVC ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--recognizing-the-glottal-stop-as-a-phonemic-consonant⟧, but also argues that positing */'/* before all vowel-initial syllables is uneconomical because it requires deletion rules at various stages of word formation to account for pitch accent in words like *parunpe* ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--setting-up-a-glottal-stop-phoneme-before-all⟧. The phonological status of the glottal stop remains unclear in the Chitose dialect ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--the-phonological-status-of-the-glottal-stop-is⟧.
text.ja: 声門閉鎖音の音韻的地位については見解が分かれている。中川は、声門閉鎖音は独立した音素ではなく母音の前に音節の区切りを示す音声的境界指標であり、単一形態素形式において対立的機能を持たないと主張する⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--glottal-stop-boundary-marker-not-phoneme⟧⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--in-ainu-the-glottal-stop-has-no-contrastive⟧。中川はまた、Refsing（1986）がアイヌ語における声門閉鎖音の存在そのものを認めていないと報告し⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--kirsten-refsing-1986-does-not-recognize-the-existence⟧、Refsing自身も浅井（1969）が声門閉鎖という特徴を認めながらも独立した音素としては扱っていないと報告している⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--asai-1969-recognizes-glottal-closure-seimon-heisa-but⟧。一方でRefsingは、服部（1964）がすべての語頭母音の前および母音間に声門破裂音/ʔ/を立て、これを独立した子音音素*'*として扱っていると報告しており⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--hattori-1964-posits-a-glottal-plosive-before-all⟧、中川も1950年代に服部四郎と田村すゞ子がすべての母音の前に声門破裂音を認め、これを子音音素として認定したと報告している⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--in-the-1950s-shiro-hattori-and-suzuko-tamura⟧。佐藤は、語頭母音の前および母音間に声門閉鎖音を音素として立てることができると提案する⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--glottal-stop-can-be-analyzed-as-a-phoneme⟧。中川は、声門破裂音を音素として認めると北海道アイヌ語の音節構造がCVとCVCの2つに簡略化されると指摘しつつ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--recognizing-the-glottal-stop-as-a-phonemic-consonant⟧、*parunpe*のような語のアクセントを説明するために各段階で*/'/*を削除する規則が必要となり記述上経済的ではないとも論じる⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--setting-up-a-glottal-stop-phoneme-before-all⟧。千歳方言においては声門閉鎖音の音韻的地位は明確ではない⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--the-phonological-status-of-the-glottal-stop-is⟧。

text.en: In Hokkaido southwest dialects, /ʔ/ tends to weaken in intervocalic positions but does not weaken in accented syllables ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--the-glottal-stop-tends-to-weaken-in-intervocalic⟧, and in Saru Ainu specifically, the glottal stop is often omitted in the syllable immediately following an accented syllable ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--in-saru-ainu-the-glottal-stop-is-often⟧. A glottal stop or tension is clearly audible when V2 bears accent and/or when V2 is followed by a consonant in a closed syllable ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--a-glottal-stop-or-tension-is-clearly-audible⟧, whereas when V2 does not bear accent and is not in a closed syllable, no clear glottal stop is audible and the transition between the two vowels is gradual ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--when-v2-does-not-bear-accent-and-is⟧. When the suffixes *-as* and *-an* attach to verbs ending in a consonant other than *n*, a glottal stop may be inserted before them, whereas after verbs ending in *n* they are generally pronounced continuously ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--when-the-suffixes-as-and-an-attach-to⟧.
text.ja: 北海道南西方言では、/ʔ/は母音間において弱化する傾向があるが、アクセントのある音節では弱化しない⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--the-glottal-stop-tends-to-weaken-in-intervocalic⟧。特に沙流アイヌ語では、声門閉鎖音はアクセントのある音節の直後の音節においてしばしば脱落する⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--in-saru-ainu-the-glottal-stop-is-often⟧。V2にアクセントがある場合、および／またはV2が閉音節にあり後続子音を伴う場合、声門閉鎖音（または緊張）が明瞭に聞き取れる⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--a-glottal-stop-or-tension-is-clearly-audible⟧。一方、V2にアクセントがなく閉音節でもない場合、明瞭な声門閉鎖音は聞こえず、2つの母音間の移行は緩慢である⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--when-v2-does-not-bear-accent-and-is⟧。*-as*・*-an*は、*n*以外の子音で終わる動詞に付く場合は声門閉鎖音を入れて発音されることがあり、*n*で終わる動詞に付く場合は続けて発音されるのが一般的である⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--when-the-suffixes-as-and-an-attach-to⟧。

text.en: In the 1950s, Shiro Hattori and Suzuko Tamura recognized the glottal stop as a phonemic consonant occurring before all vowels in Ainu ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--in-the-1950s-shiro-hattori-and-suzuko-tamura⟧.
text.ja: 1950年代に服部四郎と田村すゞ子は、アイヌ語のすべての母音の前に声門破裂音があるとし、これを子音の音素として認定した⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--in-the-1950s-shiro-hattori-and-suzuko-tamura⟧。

text.en: A sound change or alternation *s* → *h* occurs in certain words ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--the-sound-change-or-alternation-s-h-occurs⟧. In Sakhalin Ainu, when morphophonemic */h/* is followed by a vowel or *y-*, an underlying plosive or liquid — *-t-*, *-p-*, *-k-*, or *-r-* — surfaces ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--when-morphophonemic-h-is-followed-by-a-vowel⟧.
text.ja: 語によって*s*から*h*への交替（s→h）が見られる⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--the-sound-change-or-alternation-s-h-occurs⟧。樺太アイヌ語では、形態音素*/h/*の後に母音や*y-*が続くと、本来の子音である*-t-*、*-p-*、*-k-*、*-r-*が現れる⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--when-morphophonemic-h-is-followed-by-a-vowel⟧。

text.en: The phoneme /h/ shows considerable variation across dialects and prosodic environments. In Hokkaido southwest dialects, /h/ is hardly distinguishable in intervocalic position, where it is frequently weakened and voiced to [ɦ] ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--the-phoneme-h-is-hardly-distinguishable-in-intervocalic⟧, and before /u/ it is often realized as a voiceless bilabial fricative [ɸ] ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--before-u-h-is-often-realized-as-a⟧; in Sakhalin Ainu, /h/ is [h] at syllable onset, sometimes voiced [ɦ] intervocalically, [ɦ]~[ç] after /i/ in coda, [ɸ] after /u/ in coda, and after other vowels a voiceless breath with the shape of the preceding vowel ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--h-is-h-at-syllable-onset-sometimes-voiced⟧. More generally, the fricative *h* palatalizes to [ç] before *i* and labializes toward [F] before *u*, while remaining the same phoneme ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--the-fricative-h-palatalizes-to-before-i-and⟧. Cases of h-insertion are restricted to specific morphological contexts such as possessive formation ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--cases-of-h-insertion-are-restricted-to-specific⟧. Across word boundaries, an initial *hV-* sequence can drop *h-* after a consonant-final word ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--across-word-boundaries-an-initial-hv-sequence-can⟧, and particles and formal nouns beginning with *h-* or *y-* often drop the initial consonant and are pronounced continuously with the preceding word ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--particles-and-formal-nouns-beginning-with-h-or⟧. In the Shizunai dialect, the [h] of the nominalizer *hi* is usually elided in all but very slow speech ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--shizunai-hi-initial-h-deletion⟧; initial *h-* of unstressed suffixes tends to disappear without exception in rapid speech and almost always in normal speech unless there is a pause or hesitation ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--initial-h-tends-to-disappear-in-unstressed-suffixes⟧; *hine* frequently drops word-initial [h], and in rapid speech [i] may also drop so that only [ne] remains ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--in-the-pronunciation-of-hine-word-initial-h⟧; and *hike* similarly tends to drop initial [h] in rapid speech ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--hike-tends-to-drop-the-initial-h-in⟧. In Hokkaido more broadly, in normal-speed speech the word-initial *h-* of *hine* is not pronounced, and *i-* often forms a single syllable with the coda consonant of the preceding word ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--in-normal-speed-speech-word-initial-h-of⟧. In dialects such as Tokachi, Eastern Hokkaido, and Ishikari, initial *h* has a strong tendency not to occur, especially at the beginning of unaccented words ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--in-dialects-such-as-tokachi-eastern-hokkaido-and⟧, and in Tokachi, Kushiro, and Ishikari, unaccented word-initial *h-* regularly drops ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--in-dialects-such-as-tokachi-kushiro-and-ishikari⟧; in the Ishikari dialect specifically, *hine* may be written as *ine* ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--in-dialects-such-as-ishikari-where-word-initial⟧. When accent falls on the second syllable because the first syllable is open, word-initial /h/ is often elided in geographically eastern dialects ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--when-accent-falls-on-the-second-syllable-because⟧. Conversely, in the Urakawa and Samani dialects there is a tendency to add an initial *h-* to words that begin with a vowel in other dialects ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--in-the-urakawa-and-samani-dialects-there-is⟧, and insertion of word-initial /h/ is prominent in unaccented-type dialects in the northeastern part of Hokkaido ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--insertion-of-word-initial-h-is-prominent-in⟧. In Bihoro, initial syllables that had high pitch accent in Proto-Hokkaido Ainu developed a prothetic */h-/*, while those with low pitch did not ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--in-bihoro-initial-syllables-that-had-high-pitch⟧. Early sources of Kuril Ainu attest both prothetic *h-* and the loss of original *h-* ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--early-sources-of-kuril-ainu-attest-both-prothetic⟧.
text.ja: 音素/h/は方言および韻律環境によって大きく変異する。北海道南西方言では、/h/は母音間においてほとんど聞き分けられず、しばしば弱化して有声化し[ɦ]になり⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--the-phoneme-h-is-hardly-distinguishable-in-intervocalic⟧、/u/の前ではしばしば無声両唇摩擦音[ɸ]として実現する⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--before-u-h-is-often-realized-as-a⟧。樺太アイヌ語では、/h/は音節頭では[h]（母音間では有声の[ɦ]になることがある）、音節末では/i/の後で[ɦ]〜[ç]、/u/の後で[ɸ]、それ以外の母音後では前の母音と同じ口の形の弱い息となる⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--h-is-h-at-syllable-onset-sometimes-voiced⟧。より一般的に、摩擦音*h*は*i*と結合するとき口蓋化して[ç]に、*u*と結合するとき唇音化して[F]に近づくが、同一の音素である⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--the-fricative-h-palatalizes-to-before-i-and⟧。h挿入の事例は所有形形成などの特定の形態論的文脈に限定される⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--cases-of-h-insertion-are-restricted-to-specific⟧。語境界を越えて、子音終わりの語の後では語頭の*hV-*連続から*h-*が脱落することがある⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--across-word-boundaries-an-initial-hv-sequence-can⟧。*h-*や*y-*で始まる助詞や形式名詞はその音が脱落して前の語と連続して発音されることが多い⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--particles-and-formal-nouns-beginning-with-h-or⟧。静内方言では、形式名詞*hi*の語頭[h]は極めて遅い発話を除いて通常脱落し⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--shizunai-hi-initial-h-deletion⟧、無強勢の接尾辞における語頭*h-*は早口では例外なく、通常の発話でも休止やためらいがない限りほぼ常に脱落する⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--initial-h-tends-to-disappear-in-unstressed-suffixes⟧。*hine*では語頭の[h]が頻繁に脱落し、早口では[i]も脱落して[ne]のみが残ることがある⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--in-the-pronunciation-of-hine-word-initial-h⟧。*hike*も早口において語頭の[h]を脱落させる傾向がある⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--hike-tends-to-drop-the-initial-h-in⟧。北海道全般では、通常のスピードの発話において*hine*の語頭*h-*は発音されず、*i-*が前の語の末尾子音とひとつの音節をなして発音されることが多い⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--in-normal-speed-speech-word-initial-h-of⟧。十勝・道東・石狩などの方言では特にアクセントのない語頭に*h*が立たない傾向が強く⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--in-dialects-such-as-tokachi-eastern-hokkaido-and⟧、十勝・釧路・石狩ではアクセントのない語頭の*h-*が規則的に脱落する⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--in-dialects-such-as-tokachi-kushiro-and-ishikari⟧。石狩方言では*hine*が*ine*と記されることもある⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--in-dialects-such-as-ishikari-where-word-initial⟧。第1音節が開音節であるために第2音節にアクセントが落ちる場合、地理的により東方の方言において語頭の/h/が脱落することが多い⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--when-accent-falls-on-the-second-syllable-because⟧。一方、浦河・様似方言では他方言で母音始まりである語頭に*h-*を加える傾向があり⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--in-the-urakawa-and-samani-dialects-there-is⟧、語頭/h/の添加は北海道北東部に位置する無アクセント型方言において顕著である⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--insertion-of-word-initial-h-is-prominent-in⟧。美幌方言では、祖北海道アイヌ語で高ピッチアクセントを持っていた語頭音節に前置的*/h-/*が発生したが、低ピッチ音節には発生しなかった⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--in-bihoro-initial-syllables-that-had-high-pitch⟧。千島アイヌ語の初期資料は前置的*h-*の存在と本来の*h-*の消失の双方を証拠づけている⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--early-sources-of-kuril-ainu-attest-both-prothetic⟧。

text.en: The occurrence of /h/ in coda position is treated differently across dialects and analyses. Refsing asserts that /h/ is not found as a final consonant in Hokkaido Ainu, where it often becomes [ɸ] before */-u/* ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--the-weak-fricative-h-often-becomes-before-u⟧. In Sakhalin Ainu, by contrast, syllable-final */-h/* after */i/* is phonetically neutralized with */-s/*, fluctuating between [ɕ] and [ʃ] but usually closer to [ʃ] ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--after-i-syllable-final-h-is-phonetically-neutralized⟧, and Nakagawa similarly notes that syllable-final *-x* (*-h*) in Sakhalin Ainu, when preceded by *i*, may be pronounced from a sound close to [çi] to a sound transcribed by small ㇱ ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--in-sakhalin-ainu-syllable-final-x-h-after⟧. Morpheme-initial *h-* is deleted after *-n* in Sakhalin Ainu, and word-initial *h-* can alternate with glottal stop plus vowel (*'V-*) ⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--morpheme-initial-h-is-deleted-after-n-and⟧.
text.ja: 音節末における/h/の出現は方言および分析によって異なる扱いを受けている。Refsing は北海道アイヌ語において/h/は音節末子音としては現れず、*/-u/*の前でしばしば[ɸ]となると主張する⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--the-weak-fricative-h-often-becomes-before-u⟧。一方、樺太アイヌ語では音節末の*/-h/*は*/i/*の後に来た場合に*/-s/*と中和されて発音され、[ɕ]と[ʃ]の間を動揺するが[ʃ]に近く発音されることが多く⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--after-i-syllable-final-h-is-phonetically-neutralized⟧、中川も樺太方言の音節末*-x*（*-h*）は直前に*i*が来た場合にヒに近い音から小文字のㇱで書き表されるような音で発音される場合があると指摘する⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--in-sakhalin-ainu-syllable-final-x-h-after⟧。樺太アイヌ語では形態素頭の*h-*は*-n*の後で消去され、語頭の*h-*は*'V-*になることがある⟦claim:phon/glottal-stop--morpheme-initial-h-is-deleted-after-n-and⟧。
